clue.text: I'm a shellfish at heart

parts.note: the speaker is a small edible bivalve, and the phrase 'warm the ___s of one's heart' means to give deep pleasure, so the shellfish lives 'at heart'

explanation.surface: A creature confesses that deep down it is really a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'warms the cockles of the heart' means it brings inner joy; the clue treats those heart-cockles as real shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockle is a small edible bivalve mollusc, and the idiom places them in the heart.

clue.text: Little room for love with this in your hand?

definitions.text: Little room for love with this in your hand?

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
love is nil in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A question about a cramped space where romance might happen while holding something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the instrument: little room is left for a sweetheart when you are holding this big stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist holds the large bowed instrument between the knees with bow in hand.

clue.text: Curries cooked in ship

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of the word before it are prepared afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cooks a curry dinner on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruiser is a type of warship or pleasure boat.

clue.text: Clark boots end with Clark, upset, taking a whole gun

indicators.note: upset means the gathered letters are knocked over and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A shooting story: Clark gets his boots kicked over while handling a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the eighteen letters of CLARK BOOTS END plus CLARK; 'with' and 'taking' are link words. The phrase names the three main parts of an old firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: The firing mechanism, wooden butt and tube are the three parts of a musket, so the phrase means the entire weapon, hence everything.

clue.text: Frank's present ability based on past performance?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece resting on another means it follows directly after it

parts.note: 'can' expresses ability in the present tense
'did' is the past tense of do, a performance in the past

explanation.surface: A remark on whether talent now rests on a track record.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'Frank's' stands for 'is' and is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid and frank are synonyms meaning open and honest.

clue.text: Nod to a republican line?

parts.note: a nod signals assent, as when a party member assents to the official line laid down by the leadership

explanation.surface: A politician gives a small nod towards the party position.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding is a gesture of assent, and to concur with a party line is to assent to it.

clue.text: Mother's getting on with legal compensation

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse; the 's is no letter
to age is to grow older, to get on in years

explanation.surface: A mother growing old pursues a compensation claim in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Damages are money awarded by a court to make good a loss.

clue.text: Predatory insect renders Spooner's bottle empty!

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words are exchanged

parts.note: a flagon is a large bottle for wine or cider
dry means empty, drained of liquid

explanation.surface: An insect's arrival is pictured as an empty drinking bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: FLAGON DRY with the starts FL and DR exchanged gives DRAGON FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The dragonfly hunts other flying insects on the wing.

clue.text: Ruffle when ruffled?

definitions.meaning: a gathered strip of fabric sewn onto a skirt or curtain as trimming
what someone in a huff does: storms out with exaggerated movements

explanation.surface: A frilly trim and a person who has been annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathered frill on a garment, and also to storm off in a temper when one's feathers are ruffled.

clue.text: Lines needing a lot of electric power when carrier's about

indicators.note: about means the carrier goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a tray carries things; the 's is 'is'
MW, a megawatt, is a large unit of electric power

explanation.surface: Railway lines that consume huge amounts of electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and MW inside TRAY. 'needing' and 'when' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramway is the set of rails along which trams run.

clue.text: See 20
Nous sons" — see her translation

indicators.note: a translation turns words into a different form, here a new order of the letters

explanation.surface: A quoted French phrase is offered up for someone to translate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nous' looks like French 'we' but is the English word for common sense; 'translation' rearranges SONS and SEE HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British slang for practical good judgment, the same as common sense.

clue.text: Politeness of people on the way out keeping nomad diverted

indicators.note: keeping means the first piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: goners are people about to die or depart

indicators.note: diverted means the letters of the word are sent off on a different path, rearranged

explanation.surface: Dying people politely keep a wandering traveller amused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts ODMAN, a rearrangement of NOMAD from 'diverted', inside GONERS. The grid prints GOON, but the wordplay and the phrase need GOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtesy and polite behaviour are what good etiquette means.

clue.text: Freight for century old ship

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Goods carried aboard a hundred-year-old vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is goods carried by ship or plane, the same as freight.

clue.text: In company I'm greeting an outbreak of wrongdoing

indicators.note: In means the next piece is set inside the company

parts.note: a crew is a company of people working together
ave is the Latin for hail, a greeting

explanation.surface: Someone says hello in company just as a spate of crime breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden rise in the number of crimes in an area is called a crime wave.

clue.text: Exercise taxonomy on the small ads?

definitions.text: Exercise taxonomy on the small ads?

parts.words: Exercise taxonomy on the small ads?
parts.note: taxonomy is sorting into categories, and the small ads in a newspaper are called classifieds, so sorting them is what the verb asks

explanation.surface: A zoologist's urge to sort species turned on newspaper ads.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxonomy is the arranging of things into categories, and small ads are known as classifieds.

clue.text: See 3
Obfuscation leading one to knowledge? Wrong

indicators.note: leading means the first piece goes in front of the rest

parts.note: a mist obscures and confuses, as obfuscation does
A is the indefinite article, meaning one
ken is range of knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: Muddled thinking leads someone towards knowledge, but they end up in error.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaken means in error, the same as wrong.

clue.text: Bird on an island meets a fairy

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A small bird on an island encounters a fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Ulster's place on the woolsack?

definitions.meaning: a city and county in Northern Ireland, the province often called Ulster
the Woolsack is the Lord Chancellor's seat in the House of Lords; Lord Irvine, Lord Chancellor 1997-2003, was known by this nickname

explanation.surface: Asking where an Ulster town sits in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Woolsack is the wool-stuffed cushion the Lord Chancellor sits on in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: A Northern Irish city also called Londonderry, and the nickname of Lord Chancellor Alexander Irvine.

clue.text: Singer dressed

definitions.meaning: Paul ..., the American bass-baritone singer and actor
having one's gowns on, read as two words

explanation.surface: A vocalist gets clothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Robeson was a celebrated bass singer, and split as 'robes on' the name means clothed.

clue.text: Gave up privilege and money held by French boy all over the place

parts.note: left means departed from, gave up a place or job
a right is an entitlement or privilege

indicators.note: held by means the money sits inside the boy's name

parts.note: Andre is a common French boy's name
a cent is a coin, a small unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone renounces status and wealth as a French lad scatters it everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' in the clue is a link word; the AND of the answer comes from ANDRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means everywhere, in every direction, from all sides of the political map.

clue.text: Commercial lawyers in number are hackneyed

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the number

parts.note: three is a number
an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: Business lawyers in a group are a tired old cliche.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare means worn out and overused, the same as hackneyed.

clue.text: Time to enter digit is a pain

indicators.note: to enter means this goes into the next piece

parts.note: a toe is a digit of the foot
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A stubbed toe hurts for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A throe is a violent spasm of pain, as in death throes.

clue.text: See 20
See 12
Give warning of grease applied to top of pole

indicators.note: top of means only the first letter of the following word is taken
applied means the grease is worked and spread about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone smears grease on the top of a pole, perhaps for a fairground climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foretell or be a sign of something coming.

clue.text: I cancel the Times — Queen

parts.note: eras are times, periods of history
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A reader cancels their subscription to the Times newspaper, signed by the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Times' looks like the newspaper but means plain periods.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber removes pencil marks, so it is something that cancels writing.

clue.text: Our world — don't leave it to chance, I say

indicators.note: I say signals that the words are spoken, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: to arrange something in advance rather than trust luck is to plan it

explanation.surface: Advice about the Earth's future: organise things rather than gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the planet humans live on.
